title: Build a competing general-purpose military data fabric / data mesh platform

scores.rationale: Real, documented pain exists in the data layer (swivel-chair reconciliation, thumb-drive coalition sharing, undocumented APIs per Jailbreak, GAO classification findings), but that pain is about seams in the fielded stack. The pain this gap actually addresses - a program office wanting an alternative general-purpose platform - has no documented sufferer; Army and CDAO leaders publicly champion government-owned interfaces and multi-vendor onboarding rather than a second fabric.

Data-movement friction is daily for staffs, but the platform-level decision is made once per decade (10-year enterprise agreements, June 2026 baseline). A vendor selling a competing fabric would encounter the buying moment roughly once per program generation.

Large budgets exist in the layer (NGC2 FY27 request ~$3.78B; >$2B FY27 for Maven/JFN; $30B of enterprise-agreement ceilings), which is why this is not a 0, but every dollar is executed through designated teams and enterprise licenses; no line, RFI or solicitation for an alternative platform was found. Ceilings are not obligations.

The Army closed the competition with the June 2026 baseline and the joint level chose Maven; the only ways in are as a sub to a team lead or through SBIR/TAK/Tradewinds doors that admit components, not platforms. A 1 rather than 0 because Jailbreak, Open DAGIR and Right to Integrate do keep third-party onboarding formally open.

Open-source building blocks (CRDT sync, schema registries, protobuf/gRPC, Kubernetes at the edge) make a fabric technically buildable, but reaching parity with Lattice/Foundry (multi-level security, ATO at Secret, hundreds of adapters, SDK ecosystem) is a multi-year, multi-hundred-engineer effort.

Scored 0 because $250k cannot fund even a proof of concept of a general-purpose military data fabric: the government's own prototype OTAs for the layer were $99.6M and $26M, the incumbents' relevant contract ceilings are in the tens of billions, and a credible demo requires cleared staff and exercise access. $250k funds only a three-node open-standards component demo, which is a different gap.

A lab demo of sync/catalog features is possible in 6 months, but a demo the Army or CDAO would treat as credible for a fabric requires participation in Ivy Sting / Lightning Surge / PC-C class events under a team lead, realistically 18-36 months away for a new firm with no clearances.

Open standards (CoT/TAK, STANAG-style schemas, DMRA/UDRA public documents) and synthetic feeds support a component prototype, but the data a platform must actually handle (NGC2 API baseline, Maven ontology, program-of-record ICDs, exercise data) is CUI or vendor-gated and obtainable only via sponsorship.

Highest-burden profile in the study: CUI at minimum, Secret for division data layers, SCI for Maven feeds, ATO required, facility clearance and FOCI review for a firm with a non-U.S.-person co-founder, possible ITAR technical data for weapon/C2 adapters, SBIR eligibility in doubt. Not a 0 because an unclassified component demo on open standards remains legal and possible.

Partly: a sync/catalog component can start on open standards and synthetic data, but anything that would justify calling it a competing fabric requires classified integration immediately (classification_dependence: immediate).

Scored 0 (most intense) because the slot is occupied by designation: Anduril leads the Army baseline, Palantir owns the ontology and Maven PoR, Raft holds registries/federation, Lockheed integrates 25th ID, AFS integrates the enterprise, government-owned TAK/Open DAGIR commoditize the interface, and Ditto, Picogrid, Tangram, XRDefense and PLANK crowd the component tier. Absence of a rival platform reflects buyer consolidation, not opportunity.

Some cracks exist (Army CTO 'very high risk' security memo Oct 2025, GAO schedule/cost warning Aug 2026, Advana churn and IG findings, official lock-in concern behind Open DAGIR/R2I), but they are being addressed inside the incumbents' vehicles, not through a recompete. Not a 0 because a future administration or GAO/IG pressure could reopen the architecture.

A platform must integrate everything: Lattice SDK and Palantir OSDK are vendor-gated, program-of-record APIs remain prime-controlled even after Jailbreak documented them, and each sensor or vehicle protocol is bespoke (Shift5 took two months for one telemetry integration). A new entrant would face every seam with none of the incumbents' access.

The government intends to own the interfaces (UDRA, Open DAGIR, Right to Integrate) and the platform owners can absorb components; nothing a new fabric vendor builds becomes proprietary except onboarded adapters and exercise-proven deployments inside someone else's stack.

Data-mesh, registry and offline-first sync technology has a genuine commercial market (Ditto funds defense work from commercial revenue), so the technology is portable, but the commercial data-fabric market is itself dominated by Databricks, Snowflake, Confluent and hyperscalers.

If a firm somehow held the fabric slot, expansion across services and allies would be enormous (Anduril and Palantir demonstrate this), but the conditional is not credible; realistic expansion is that of a component riding a platform owner's growth.

Enterprise software licenses and task orders in this layer recur annually under the enterprise agreements and Maven's ceiling raises show demand exceeding scope; the recurring revenue is real, it just accrues to the designated vendors.

Scored 0 because nothing the platform play requires matches the team: no cleared U.S.-citizen personnel (neither founder can currently hold a clearance), a non-U.S.-person co-founder that complicates FOCI/SBIR/deemed-export status, no program-office or exercise relationships, $250k against incumbents spending at four to five orders of magnitude more, and no prior data-platform operating experience at scale. The same team could fit a narrow open-standards component, which is scored under other gaps.

market.summary: No budget owner wants a second platform: NGC2 money executes through the June 2026 baseline team under decade-long enterprise agreements, joint money goes to Maven as program of record, enterprise money went to an integrator; the only 'demand' is government preference for owning interfaces, which favors free standards, not a new vendor. The pain is real but is felt at seams the incumbents are funded to close.

competition.summary: Anduril, Palantir and Raft do not need six months to add it; they are the designated fabric, hold the SDKs every third party must use, and can absorb any demonstrated feature. Government-owned TAK/Open DAGIR/UDRA commoditize the interface layer, and switching cost after fielding at 4th ID, 25th ID and I Corps rises every quarter.

feasibility.summary: A platform cannot be demonstrated credibly without Secret-level exercise access, an ATO, cleared staff and a facility clearance; a two-student team with a non-U.S.-person co-founder and $250k faces FOCI, SBIR-eligibility and deemed-export constraints before writing an adapter. The government's own prototype OTAs for this layer were $26M-$99.6M; a $250k MVP proves nothing a buyer would act on.

verdict_rationale: Decisive reason: the platform slot was filled by designation (Army NGC2 common data-layer baseline, June 22 2026; Maven program of record, March 2026; AFS enterprise integration, July 2026) and is locked behind 10-year enterprise agreements with $10B and $20B ceilings, so the PROBLEM -> USER -> REQUIREMENT OWNER -> PROGRAM OFFICE -> CONTRACTING OFFICE -> BUDGET -> VEHICLE chain exists but every link already terminates at Anduril/Palantir/Raft; there is no buyer, no vehicle and no feasible demo for a $250k two-student team with a non-U.S.-person co-founder. Market attractiveness 1.7 and founder fit 1.0 with the major no-path penalty applied. The registry's LOW pre-rating is confirmed; the gap should be eliminated explicitly.
narrower_version_if_borderline: Not borderline. The survivable descendants are already tracked separately as seam components sold through a team lead or a government-owned door: UDRA-conformant tactical-echelon data-product catalog for DDIL nodes (cf. G02/G05), automated conformance and contract-test tooling for the government-approved NGC2 API baseline and Jailbreak API marketplace (cf. G07), and policy-aware releasability tagging and sync for coalition enclaves (cf. G17). None of these is a 'competing data fabric'.
most_important_question_answer: With $250,000 today, two exceptionally capable founders should not build a competing data fabric at all; if they insist on this layer, the only defensible first build is a small open-standards component - a DDIL-tolerant data-product catalog and schema registry on a rugged edge node that ingests CoT/TAK and open protobuf feeds, applies releasability labels, and syncs conflict-free across partitions - demonstrated on three commercial nodes with synthetic data. They should show it to the third-party onboarding leads of the NGC2 team stacks (Anduril Lattice SDK and Lockheed/Raft teams), the TAK Product Center plugin pipeline, and an Army or Air Force SBIR TPOC, and the demo must prove that onboarding a new feed takes hours instead of the two months Shift5 needed and that nothing is lost across partition and reconnection. The customer cares because the UDRA RFI concedes the mesh stops above tactical echelons and Jailbreak showed onboarding is the bottleneck. An incumbent cannot trivially crush them only if the component is positioned as something they would rather license or acquire than rebuild, which is a licensing/acqui-hire outcome, not a platform company. The milestone that would justify $2-5M is a signed subcontract or Phase II/III with a team lead plus successful participation in an Ivy Sting / Lightning Surge class event; absent that within 12-18 months the idea fails because there is no independent buyer. As framed (a general-purpose competing fabric), it fails on day one for lack of a buyer, a vehicle and a feasible demo.
bear_case_summary: The Army just chose (June 2026), the joint level chose Maven (PoR March 2026), the enterprise chose an integrator (AFS, July 2026), and both platform owners hold decade-long vehicles with $10B and $20B ceilings; the government's stated strategy is to own interfaces, not to buy a second platform; standalone middleware startups in this layer sit in SBIR purgatory (Tangram since 2020, XRDefense $4.75M Phase III); every real integration needs CUI/Secret access, an ATO and cleared staff that a two-student, non-U.S.-person-inclusive team cannot supply; and $250k is four to five orders of magnitude below the incumbents' spend on the same layer.
bull_case_summary: Strongest honest bull case: the layer is where the money is (NGC2 ~$3.78B FY27 request, >$2B FY27 for Maven/JFN), the government has publicly conceded the seams (undocumented APIs, classification, tagging, mesh stopping at division, IG-documented enterprise ingest failures), Open DAGIR/UDRA/Right to Integrate signal official discomfort with lock-in, an Army CTO memo and GAO have flagged security and schedule risk in the chosen stack, and team leads have proven they pull small vendors in within months (Rune, Shift5, Accelint, Striveworks). Even this bull case supports a seam component with an acquisition exit, not a competing fabric.
